name: What happens if exterior remodeling work starts before permit approval?

mainEntity.name: What happens if exterior remodeling starts before the permit is approved in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What happens if exterior remodeling starts before the permit is approved in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Starting exterior remodel work before permit approval is risky because the city can require the job to stop until approvals are in place. If the work is visible or reported, inspectors may issue correction notices and require documentation, revisions, or even partial demolition to verify compliance. The impact depends on the scope, but projects involving structure, windows, doors, electrical, plumbing, or grading are especially sensitive. Even if the work looks minor, unpermitted changes can create problems later when a homeowner tries to refinance, sell, or insure the property. The safest strategy is to treat permit approval as a project milestone, not a formality. Before any demolition, homeowners should confirm whether the contractor has the correct license, whether the plans are approved, and whether the first inspection point is clear. If work has already started, the best next step is to pause, document the scope, and resolve the permit path before additional construction makes the issue larger. Fixing permit problems early is usually much cheaper than undoing completed work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Starting exterior remodeling before permit approval can trigger stop-work orders, correction notices, fines, and delayed inspections. The project may need to be opened up or redesigned to meet current code before final approval. If the work affects structure, utilities, or safety, unpermitted construction can also complicate insurance and resale.
